magisterium.assessment_en: The call to prayer, fasting, rejecting hatred, and perseverance in faith is mainly aligned with Catholic teaching; the Church explicitly warns against the ruinous nature of hatred and excessive nationalism. However, the claim that fasting and prayer cause the withdrawal of "spirits of nationalism and war" and that for a major war it is necessary for many to carry it in their hearts is stated as a certain cause-and-effect conclusion, which goes beyond what can be established from the cited sources.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Ecclesial sources support prayer, fasting, and conversion as a response to sin, hatred, and war; John Paul II particularly warns that excessive nationalism can lead to violence and vengeance, but distinguishes such nationalism from legitimate love of homeland. Jesus' words about persevering to the end are a call to fidelity through trials, not a promise that prayer or fasting will in themselves prevent a particular war.
concerns_en: Presenting a private Marian message as a confirmed fact should not suggest that it carries the same binding nature or authority as Sacred Scripture and the teaching of the Church.

Linking fasting with the retreat of "spirits of nationalism and war" may be spiritually evocative, but without additional clarification it risks presenting it as a guaranteed mechanism that removes war or its spiritual cause.
The claim that a great war requires a large number of people carrying it in their hearts oversimplifies the causes of war and is not substantiated by the cited biblical or ecclesial sources.

sections.subtitle_en: Our Lady's message on election day: hatred and war reign in the hearts of men
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host quotes Our Lady's latest message and calls for stronger prayer
sections.content_en:
Speaking about how the church is built, Grebenar refers to Our Lady's latest message and calls it „very significant“. He recalls that the Ora et Labora community, which originates from Međugorje, gathers tens of thousands of people in prayer and thousands in fasting, and is just finishing a 40-day fast against the spirits of war.

The message, as he states, arrived two or three days ago and coincided with the day of the elections in Serbia, the 25th of the month. In it, Our Lady calls for **even stronger prayer** and warns that hatred and war reign in the hearts of people. „That is so accurate. We see that across Europe now“, comments Grebenar. His interpretation is as follows: in order for a great war to happen, there must be many people who carry war in their heart. When one fasts and prays, the „spirits of nationalism and war“ depart.

Therefore, he repeats that no victory has been won and that believers face long battles to the end. He cites in this regard the words of Jesus: „The one who perseveres to the end will be saved.“

sections.subtitle: Pet obraćenih duša vrijedi više od pet milijuna pregleda
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar uspoređuje vrijednost obraćenih duša s brojem pregleda na podcastima
sections.content:
Borba između dobra i zla traje tisućama godina, a Grebenar ističe da i vjernici moraju dati svoj doprinos. Iznosi ključnu tezu ovog dijela tumačenja: **„Crkva se gradi tako da se ruše sotonine utvrde.“** Te se utvrde nalaze u srcima ljudi, a voditelj ih nabraja:

- mržnja,
- želja za ratom,
- želja za preljubom,
- želja za krađom,
- gramzivost i sebičnost.

Kad vjernici poste i mole za obraćenje drugih i za narod, te se utvrde ruše i sve više ljudi prilazi Kristu.

U nastavku Grebenar otvoreno kritizira kriterije medijskog uspjeha: „Više vrijedi pet obraćenih duša nego pet milijuna pregleda nečega na nekom podcastu.“ Pregleda može biti milijune, ali ako se ni jedna duša nije obratila i nitko nije rastao u vjeri, to prema njemu ništa ne vrijedi. Obraćenje pritom definira široko: kao rast u vjeri, otvaranje očiju i spoznaju nečega novoga.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: zlo, grijeh i napastovanje stvarni su, a molitva, post i obraćenje pripadaju kršćanskom odgovoru; naglasak na plodovima evangelizacije umjesto na pukoj popularnosti također je opravdan. Ipak, izraz „sotonine utvrde“ najbolje je razumjeti kao slikovit govor o grijehu i djelovanju zla, a ne kao oznaku za određene osobe, dok tvrdnju o vrijednosti pregleda treba shvatiti kao usporedbu prioriteta, ne kao tvrdnju da medijski doseg nema nikakvu vrijednost.
concerns: Riječ „obraćenje“ može značiti početni zaokret prema Bogu, ali i trajni rast u vjeri; pojedina nova spoznaja sama po sebi nije nužno obraćenje ako ne vodi promjeni života i vjernijem nasljedovanju Krista.
Suprotstavljanje pet obraćenih duša milijunima pregleda snažno izražava prvenstvo spasenja i duhovnog ploda, ali pregledi mogu biti sredstvo kojim se Evanđelje naviješta i dopire do ljudi.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk potvrđuje ozbiljnost grijeha i stvarnost duhovne borbe, ali naglašava da je Krist pravi Spasitelj i da se obraćenje ostvaruje njegovom otkupiteljskom djelatnošću, a ne samo ljudskim naporom. Post i molitva imaju smisla kao oslonac na Božju milost, uz ustrajnost u činjenju dobra i ljubavi prema bližnjima. Obraćenje je trajni put: važno je da navještaj donosi plodove vjere i promjene života, a ne samo mjerljivu popularnost.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mainly aligned with Catholic teaching: evil, sin, and temptation are real, and prayer, fasting, and conversion belong to the Christian response; the emphasis on the fruits of evangelization instead of mere popularity is also justified. However, the phrase "Satan's strongholds" is best understood as figurative speech about sin and the activity of evil, rather than as a designation for specific persons, while the claim about the value of views should be understood as a comparison of priorities, not as a claim that media reach has no value whatsoever.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching confirms the gravity of sin and the reality of spiritual battle, but emphasizes that Christ is the true Savior and that conversion is realized through his redemptive activity, not through human effort alone. Fasting and prayer make sense as reliance on God's grace, along with perseverance in doing good and love toward neighbors. Conversion is an ongoing journey: it is important that proclamation bears fruits of faith and change of life, not merely measurable popularity.
concerns_en: The word "conversion" can mean an initial turn toward God, but also ongoing growth in faith; a single new insight is not necessarily in itself conversion unless it leads to a change of life and a more faithful following of Christ.
Contrasting five converted souls with millions of views strongly expresses the primacy of salvation and spiritual fruit, but views can be a means by which the Gospel is proclaimed and reaches people.

sections.subtitle_en: Five converted souls are worth more than five million views
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar compares the value of converted souls with the number of views on podcasts
sections.content_en:
The battle between good and evil has lasted for thousands of years, and Grebenar emphasizes that believers too must make their contribution. He puts forward the key thesis of this part of the interpretation: **„The church is built by tearing down Satan's strongholds.“** Those strongholds are located in the hearts of people, and the host lists them:

- hatred,
- desire for war,
- desire for adultery,
- desire for theft,
- greed and selfishness.

When believers fast and pray for the conversion of others and for the nation, those strongholds are torn down and more and more people approach Christ.

Continuing, Grebenar openly criticizes the criteria of media success: „Five converted souls are worth more than five million views of something on some podcast.“ There may be millions of views, but if not a single soul was converted and no one grew in faith, according to him that is worth nothing. In doing so, he defines conversion broadly: as growth in faith, the opening of eyes, and the realization of something new.

sections.subtitle: Prokazivati grijeh, a ne upirati prstom u osobu
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj objašnjava razliku između osude grijeha i osude čovjeka
sections.content:
Jedino što ostaje za vječnost, poručuje Grebenar, jest **ljubav**. Ona se očituje u nesebičnom darivanju za drugoga, i to na razne načine: kroz molitvu, kroz post, ali i kroz društveni aktivizam, primjerice pisanjem tekstova na društvenim mrežama i prokazivanjem zla.

Pri tome postavlja jasnu granicu. Zlo treba prokazivati na primjeren način, a ne svađalački. Ne smije se upirati prstom u crkvu, fratre ili biskupe. „Može se uprijeti prstom u grijeh koji netko čini, ali baš uprijeti u osobu ili u instituciju, to se ne smije“, naglašava on. Istodobno upozorava da će vjernici odgovarati ako ne prokažu zlo i grijeh. Zato čovjeka uvijek treba odvojiti od grijeha.

Kao uzor navodi Isusa, koji je osudio grijeh, ali ni jednog čovjeka. Primjer je žena preljubnica: Isus je osudio grijeh, ali ne i nju. „Mi ne smijemo osuđivati druge ljude, nego osuditi grijeh“, zaključuje Grebenar.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom jer povezuje ljubav prema osobi s istinoljubivim prepoznavanjem grijeha i pozivom na obraćenje, što se vidi i u Isusovim riječima ženi: „Ni ja te ne osuđujem; idi i od sada više ne griješi” (Iv 8,11). Ipak, tvrdnja da se ne smije upirati prstom u instituciju preširoka je ako se razumije kao zabrana da se odgovorno upozori na zlo ili propust koji se u njoj događa.
concerns: Razlikovanje osobe od grijeha korisno je, ali ne bi smjelo značiti prešućivanje javnog zla ili neodgovornosti: katolička tradicija dopušta primjerenu korekciju, a ustrajno i ozbiljno javno zlo može zahtijevati da se ono iznese i pred druge ili pred Crkvu. Zato zabrana usmjerena na prokazivanje institucije treba biti ograničena osudom klevete, svađalaštva i nepromišljenog pripisivanja krivnje, a ne shvaćena kao zaštita institucije od opravdane kritike.

Formulacija da Isus nije osudio nijednog čovjeka pojednostavljuje prizor: Isus nije osudio ženu na način na koji su to htjeli njezini tužitelji, ali ju je jasno pozvao da prestane griješiti. Potrebno je razlikovati osuđivanje osobe kao da poznajemo njezino srce od moralnog prosuđivanja vidljivih postupaka i poziva na obraćenje.
magisterium.enrichment: U Ivanu 8 Isus istodobno odbacuje nasilno i licemjerno osuđivanje te ne relativizira preljub: milosrđe ženi otvara put novom životu, a ne dopušta joj da u grijehu ostane. Kršćanska ljubav zato može zahtijevati istinito imenovanje grijeha upravo radi dobra grešnika, dok upozorenje mora izbjegavati brzoplet sud o skrivenim namjerama i stanju čovjekova srca. Korekcija može biti privatna i razmjerna, a kod ustrajnog javnog grijeha može uključivati i obraćanje drugima ili Crkvi; to nije isto što i kleveta ili neprijateljsko napadanje.

citations.document_title: Who am I to Judge? Politics and the Problem of Moral Relativism
Commentary on the Gospel of John

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mainly aligned with Catholic teaching because it connects love for the person with the truthful recognition of sin and the call to conversion, as seen in Jesus' words to the woman: "Neither do I condemn you; go, and from now on sin no more" (Jn 8:11). However, the claim that one must not point a finger at an institution is too broad if understood as a prohibition against responsibly warning about evil or failure occurring within it.
magisterium.enrichment_en: In John 8, Jesus simultaneously rejects violent and hypocritical condemnation and does not relativize adultery: mercy opens the way to a new life for the woman, rather than allowing her to remain in sin. Christian love can therefore require truthfully naming sin precisely for the good of the sinner, while admonition must avoid hasty judgment about hidden intentions and the state of a person's heart. Correction can be private and proportionate, and in the case of persistent public sin it can include addressing others or the Church; this is not the same as slander or hostile attack.
concerns_en: Distinguishing the person from the sin is useful, but it should not mean remaining silent about public evil or irresponsibility: Catholic tradition allows for appropriate correction, and persistent and serious public evil may require that it be brought before others or before the Church. Therefore, the prohibition aimed at exposing an institution should be limited by the condemnation of slander, litigiousness, and reckless attribution of guilt, rather than understood as shielding an institution from justified criticism.

The formulation that Jesus did not condemn any human being oversimplifies the scene: Jesus did not condemn the woman in the manner her accusers intended, but he clearly called her to stop sinning. It is necessary to distinguish condemning a person as if knowing their heart from moral judgment of visible actions and a call to conversion.

sections.subtitle_en: Exposing sin, not pointing the finger at the person
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host explains the difference between condemning sin and condemning a person
sections.content_en:
The only thing that remains for eternity, Grebenar conveys, is **love**. It manifests itself in selfless giving for another, and that in various ways: through prayer, through fasting, but also through social activism, for example by writing texts on social networks and exposing evil.

In doing so, he establishes a clear boundary. Evil should be exposed in an appropriate manner, not in an argumentative way. One must not point a finger at the church, friars, or bishops. „One can point a finger at the sin that someone commits, but actually pointing at the person or at the institution, that is not allowed“, he emphasizes. At the same time, he warns that believers will be held accountable if they do not expose evil and sin. Therefore, man should always be separated from sin.

As a role model, he cites Jesus, who condemned sin, but not a single human being. An example is the adulterous woman: Jesus condemned the sin, but not her. „We must not condemn other people, but condemn the sin“, concludes Grebenar.

sections.subtitle: Javna isprika: voditelj priznaje vlastite slabosti
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar moli gledatelje za oprost zbog svojih pogrešaka
sections.content:
U jednom od najosobnijih trenutaka emisije Grebenar govori o kritikama na društvenim mrežama. One, kaže, mogu biti usmjerene protiv nekoga dobroga tko evangelizira, ili protiv njega samoga. „Ja nisam najbolji, ja to priznam“, kaže voditelj. Dodaje da moli Gospodina da ga obrati, učini još boljim i njegove slabosti pretvori u jakosti za Njega.

„Žao mi je zbog svih pogrešaka koje činim i koje sam napravio. Uistinu mi je žao“, govori Grebenar te se izravno obraća slušateljima: „Braćo, ja vas molim da mi oprostite.“

Iz tog priznanja izvodi pravilo. Gospodin želi da vjernici priznaju svoje slabosti i grijehe, i to javno ako je pogreška bila javna. Isto vrijedi i za prokazivanje tuđeg zla. Javno učinjeno zlo treba javno prokazati. Tajno zlo treba, kako kaže Isus, „šapnuti na uho“: najprije jednome, zatim dvojici, a onda dovesti svećenika. „Ako je nešto izašlo javno, onda se treba javno i pokajati, javno ispričati“, poručuje voditelj.

magisterium.assessment: Osobno priznanje pogrešaka, iskreno traženje oprosta i nastojanje da se popravi šteta dobro su usklađeni s kršćanskim pokajanjem. Ipak, tvrdnja da javno učinjeno zlo uvijek treba javno prokazati ili da se svaki javni grijeh mora javno ispovjediti preširoka je: primjeren način ispravka ovisi o okolnostima, a Isusov postupak u Mt 18 govori o obraćanju zajednici nakon prethodnih koraka, ne o dovođenju svećenika kao izričitom sljedećem stupnju.
concerns: Javno razotkrivanje nije univerzalno pravilo: javna opomena može biti opravdana kad je prijestup javan, šteti drugima ili je potrebna radi sprečavanja sablazni, ali bratska opomena u pravilu treba težiti obraćenju, a ne javnom posramljivanju.

Mt 18,15–17 navodi razgovor nasamo, zatim razgovor uz jednog ili dvojicu drugih, pa obraćanje crkvenoj zajednici; tekst u odlomku taj slijed pojednostavljuje i zamjenjuje posljednji korak dovođenjem svećenika.
Potrebno je razlikovati javnu ispriku za javno nanesenu štetu od tvrdnje da se svaki osobni grijeh treba javno ispovjediti; odlomak ne pravi jasno tu razliku.
magisterium.enrichment: Javno priznanje vlastite pogreške može biti čin poniznosti i istinoljubivosti, osobito kad se time priznaje povreda drugih; Crkva izričito upozorava da takvo priznanje ne ponižava ljudsko dostojanstvo. Isusov postupak u Mt 18 povezuje opomenu s nastojanjem da se brat ponovno zadobije, a cijelo poglavlje zatim naglašava oproštenje; cilj je, dakle, obraćenje i pomirenje, ne puko razotkrivanje krivca. Kad je grijeh javan, javna korekcija može biti primjerena, ali treba biti odmjerena i usmjerena na istinu, zaštitu drugih i obnovu zajedništva.

magisterium.assessment_en: Personal admission of errors, sincerely seeking forgiveness, and striving to repair damage are well aligned with Christian repentance. However, the claim that evil done publicly should always be publicly exposed or that every public sin must be publicly confessed is too broad: the appropriate mode of correction depends on circumstances, and Jesus' procedure in Mt 18 speaks of addressing the community after prior steps, not of bringing a priest as an explicit next stage.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Public admission of one's own mistake can be an act of humility and truthfulness, especially when it acknowledges harm done to others; the Church explicitly notes that such admission does not diminish human dignity. Jesus' procedure in Mt 18 links admonition with the effort to regain the brother, and the entire chapter then emphasizes forgiveness; the goal, therefore, is conversion and reconciliation, not mere exposure of the guilty party. When sin is public, public correction may be appropriate, but it should be measured and oriented toward truth, protecting others, and restoring communion.
concerns_en: Public exposure is not a universal rule: public admonition may be justified when an offense is public, harms others, or is necessary to prevent scandal, but fraternal correction should as a rule strive for conversion, not public shaming.

Mt 18:15–17 mentions speaking privately, then speaking with one or two others, then telling the church community; the text in the passage oversimplifies that sequence and replaces the last step with bringing a priest.
It is necessary to distinguish a public apology for publicly inflicted harm from the claim that every personal sin must be publicly confessed; the passage does not clearly make that distinction.

sections.subtitle_en: Public apology: host admits his own weaknesses
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar asks viewers for forgiveness because of his mistakes
sections.content_en:
In one of the most personal moments of the show, Grebenar speaks about criticism on social networks. That criticism, he says, can be directed against someone good who is evangelizing, or against himself. „I am not the best, I admit that“, says the host. He adds that he prays to the Lord to convert him, make him even better, and turn his weaknesses into strengths for Him.

„I am sorry for all the mistakes that I make and that I have made. I am truly sorry“, Grebenar says and addresses the listeners directly: „Brothers, I ask you to forgive me.“

From that admission he derives a rule. The Lord wants believers to admit their weaknesses and sins, and that publicly if the mistake was public. The same applies to exposing someone else's evil. Publicly committed evil should be exposed publicly. Secret evil should, as Jesus says, be „whispered in the ear“: first to one, then to two, and then bring a priest. „If something has come out publicly, then one should also repent publicly, apologize publicly“, conveys the host.

sections.subtitle: Strog prema grijehu, nježan prema grešniku
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj govori o grešnicima kao ranjenim ljudima kojima treba pomoć, a ne osuda
sections.content:
Kristova crkva, prema Grebenaru, širi se i naziđuje u ljubavi, praštanju i miru. Kad je potrebno, to se čini s nježnošću, a kad je potrebno, s hrabrošću. Formulu sažima ovako: **„Treba biti vrlo strog na grijeh, a vrlo nježan i blag prema grešniku.“**

Grešnici su, objašnjava on, ranjeni ljudi kojima treba pomoć, a ne osuda. Za učinak osude služi se slikovitom usporedbom: osuđeni čovjek osjeća se „kao mačka koja je stjerana u kut“ i mora se braniti. Bog nije osudio nikoga. Ljudi, prema njegovu tumačenju, osuđuju sami sebe svojim nedjelima i odbacivanjem Boga. „Bog nas nije odbacio. Bog je sebe odbacio na križu da bismo mi bili spašeni“, ističe Grebenar.

Zatim čita psalam iz dnevnih čitanja: „Nebesa slavu Božju kazuju, nebeski svod navješćuje djelo ruku njegovih. Dan danu to objavljuje, a noć noći glas predaje.“ Psalam završava slikom jeke koja se razliježe po svoj zemlji, sve do kraja svijeta.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak na treba odbacivati grijeh, a grešniku pristupati milosrdno i pomagati mu, uglavnom je u skladu s katoličkim razumijevanjem Božjeg milosrđa. Ipak, tvrdnje da Bog „nije osudio nikoga” i da je „sebe odbacio na križu” zahtijevaju važno pojašnjenje kako ne bi zanijekale Božji sud ili pogrešno opisale Kristovu žrtvu.
concerns: Tvrdnja „Bog nije osudio nikoga” preširoka je ako znači da Bog ne sudi grijehu ili da konačna osuda nije moguća: Krist je došao da se svijet spasi, ali Evanđelje govori i o sudu koji se očituje u čovjekovu prihvaćanju ili odbacivanju svjetla; čovjekove odluke i djela imaju stvarne posljedice.

Izraz „Bog je sebe odbacio na križu” teološki je neprecizan ako se shvati doslovno. Katolički nauk govori o tome da je Otac predao Sina za spasenje svijeta i da je Krist nosio grijehe čovječanstva, a ne o tome da je Bog odbacio samoga sebe.
magisterium.enrichment: Milosrđe ne znači ravnodušnost prema zlu: Krist susreće grešnika radi spasenja, ali poziva na obraćenje i napuštanje grijeha. Križ istodobno objavljuje Božju ljubav i ozbiljnost grijeha, a čovjek je pozvan ispitati svoj život u Kristovu svjetlu. Citirani psalam vjerno naviješta da nebesa objavljuju Božju slavu i da se njihov glas razliježe po zemlji.

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis that one must reject sin while approaching the sinner mercifully and helping him is mainly aligned with the Catholic understanding of God's mercy. However, the claims that God "condemned no one" and that he "rejected himself on the cross" require important clarification so as not to deny God's judgment or mischaracterize Christ's sacrifice.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Mercy does not mean indifference toward evil: Christ encounters the sinner for the sake of salvation, but calls for conversion and abandoning sin. The Cross simultaneously reveals God's love and the seriousness of sin, and man is called to examine his life in the light of Christ. The cited psalm faithfully proclaims that the heavens declare the glory of God and that their voice goes out through all the earth.
concerns_en: The claim "God condemned no one" is too broad if it means that God does not judge sin or that final condemnation is impossible: Christ came that the world might be saved, but the Gospel also speaks of judgment manifested in man's acceptance or rejection of the light; human decisions and deeds have real consequences.

The expression "God rejected himself on the cross" is theologically imprecise if taken literally. Catholic teaching speaks of the Father giving up the Son for the salvation of the world and of Christ bearing the sins of humanity, not of God rejecting himself.

sections.subtitle_en: Strict toward sin, gentle toward the sinner
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host speaks about sinners as wounded people who need help, not condemnation
sections.content_en:
Christ's church, according to Grebenar, spreads and is built up in love, forgiveness, and peace. When necessary, this is done with tenderness, and when necessary, with courage. He summarizes the formula like this: **„One must be very strict toward sin, and very gentle and mild toward the sinner.“**

Sinners are, he explains, wounded people who need help, not condemnation. For the effect of condemnation he uses a vivid comparison: a condemned man feels „like a cat backed into a corner“ and has to defend himself. God has not condemned anyone. People, according to his interpretation, condemn themselves by their misdeeds and rejection of God. „God did not reject us. God rejected himself on the cross so that we might be saved“, Grebenar emphasizes.

Then he reads a psalm from the daily readings: „The heavens declare the glory of God; the skies proclaim the work of his hands. Day unto day pours forth speech; night unto night reveals knowledge.“ The psalm ends with the image of an echo resounding through all the earth, unto the ends of the world.

sections.subtitle: Problem se ne rješava načinom koji ga je stvorio
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar objašnjava poslovno pravilo i potrebu za duhovnom dimenzijom u rješavanju problema
sections.content:
Tko želi zidati crkvu i privoditi duše Kristu tako da im se mijenja život, mora drugačije govoriti, poručuje Grebenar. Tu se oslanja na pravilo iz poslovnog svijeta: način razmišljanja, ponašanja i djelovanja koji je doveo do problema ne može biti način koji će taj problem riješiti. Zato ljudi često ne uspijevaju riješiti probleme, primjerice u svojim brakovima i bračnim zajednicama.

Rješenje vidi u drugačijem pristupu. Treba moliti Boga za širi pogled i širu perspektivu, kako bi Duh Sveti uveo čovjeka u svu istinu. Tada Bog daje svoju riječ, a čovjek spoznaje da nije dovoljno stvari samo svjetovno tumačiti. Potrebna je i **duhovna dimenzija**, koju Grebenar smatra „puno važnijom“ jer dolazi od Duha Svetoga.

Usporedbu preuzima iz znanosti. Kad se otvori ta dimenzija, čovjek „ima još varijabli“, dodatne čimbenike i okolnosti, pa problem vidi na drugačiji način. Bog mu tada pokazuje kako se problem rješava i gdje je njegova vlastita odgovornost. „Svaka sotonina utvrda u životu pojedinca, obitelji i naroda je problem“, zaključuje voditelj. Poziv vjernicima stoga glasi: rješavati probleme, odnosno rušiti te utvrde.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naglaskom na molitvi, vodstvu Duha Svetoga, obraćenju i osobnoj odgovornosti, a opravdano upozorava da se problemi ne mogu uvijek razumjeti samo na površnoj ili svjetovnoj razini. Ipak, tvrdnja da je duhovna dimenzija „puno važnija” te opis problema kao sotoninih utvrda zahtijevaju razborito tumačenje kako se ne bi zanemarili ljudski, psihološki ili društveni uzroci niti olako pripisivala zloduhovska prisutnost.
concerns: Suprotstavljanje duhovne perspektive svjetovnom tumačenju može zvučati kao da su ljudsko iskustvo, razumno razmatranje i istraživanje manje važni ili suvišni; katolički pristup traži razlučivanje i priznaje potrebu kritičke procjene činjenica.

Nazivanje svake sotonine utvrde problemom može biti korisna duhovna metafora, ali ne bi smjelo voditi zaključku da su svi bračni ili obiteljski problemi izravno uzrokovani đavlom. Crkva upozorava da se napast đavla ne smije olako rabiti kao izgovor te da su potrebni suzdržanost i razboritost.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk potvrđuje stvarnost duhovne borbe i važnost molitve, ali istodobno čuva ljudsku slobodu: đavao može napastovati, no ne može prisiliti čovjeka da pristane na zlo. Duh Sveti vodi prema obraćenju, istini i odgovornom djelovanju, pa duhovno razlučivanje treba pomoći čovjeku da prepozna vlastiti udio i izabere dobro, a ne zamijeniti pažljivu procjenu konkretnih okolnosti.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mainly aligned with Catholic emphasis on prayer, the guidance of the Holy Spirit, conversion, and personal responsibility, and it rightly warns that problems cannot always be understood merely on a superficial or worldly level. However, the claim that the spiritual dimension is "much more important" and the description of problems as Satan's strongholds require prudent interpretation so as not to neglect human, psychological, or social causes nor rashly attribute a demonic presence.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching affirms the reality of spiritual battle and the importance of prayer, but at the same time safeguards human freedom: the devil can tempt, but cannot compel man to consent to evil. The Holy Spirit leads toward conversion, truth, and responsible action, so spiritual discernment should help man recognize his own part and choose the good, rather than replace careful assessment of concrete circumstances.
concerns_en: Contrasting the spiritual perspective with worldly interpretation can sound as though human experience, reasoned consideration, and investigation are less important or superfluous; the Catholic approach calls for discernment and recognizes the need for critical evaluation of facts.

Calling every stronghold of Satan a problem may be a useful spiritual metaphor, but it should not lead to the conclusion that all marital or family problems are directly caused by the devil. The Church warns that temptation from the devil should not be lightly used as an excuse, and that restraint and prudence are needed.

sections.subtitle_en: A problem is not solved by the way that created it
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar explains a business rule and the need for a spiritual dimension in problem-solving
sections.content_en:
Whoever wants to build the church and bring souls to Christ in such a way that their life changes must speak differently, Grebenar conveys. Here he relies on a rule from the business world: the way of thinking, behaving, and acting that led to a problem cannot be the way that will solve that problem. That is why people often fail to solve problems, for example in their marriages and marital unions.

He sees the solution in a different approach. One should pray to God for a wider view and a broader perspective, so that the Holy Spirit may lead man into all truth. Then God gives his word, and man realizes that it is not enough to interpret things only in a worldly manner. A **spiritual dimension** is also needed, which Grebenar considers „much more important“ because it comes from the Holy Spirit.

He borrows a comparison from science. When that dimension opens up, a person „has more variables“, additional factors and circumstances, and so sees the problem in a different way. God then shows him how the problem is solved and where his own responsibility lies. „Every stronghold of Satan in the life of an individual, a family, and a nation is a problem“, concludes the host. The call to believers is therefore: solve problems, that is, tear down those strongholds.

sections.subtitle: Đavlova računica: zašto sotona nastoji srušiti crkvu
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj opisuje borbu crkve i đavlove anticrkve i đavlovu jedinu šansu za opstanak
sections.content:
Grebenar zatim opisuje dvije sukobljene strane. „Đavlu je problem crkva. On ne zna što bi s crkvom, on bi je uništio“, kaže on. Za katolike i kršćane, s druge strane, problem je **đavlova anticrkva**: grijeh i zlo. Vjernici su pozvani u ime Kristovo razarati sotonina grešna djela, dok je đavlova zadaća razarati crkvu. Na pitanje tko će pobijediti, voditelj odgovara: onaj koji ima jaču vjeru. Dodaje i Gospine riječi da slijedi konačna bitka između dobra i zla. Krist je đavla pobijedio, ali crkva, odnosno svi vjernici, to tek trebaju učiniti.

Voditelj potom slikovito rekonstruira „đavlovu računicu“. Đavao zna da ga je Krist pobijedio za sva vremena i da se u raj više ne može vratiti. Jedina mu je šansa da izbjegne ognjenu peć zauvijek da sruši crkvu na zemlji. Kad bi u tome uspio, prema Grebenaru bi Isusova žrtva na križu za čovječanstvo od tog trenutka postala bezvrijedna. Tko se do tada spasio, spasio se, ali bi nakon toga tama zavladala. Grebenar čak iznosi pretpostavku da bi đavao tim uspjehom računao na izazivanje pobune u raju.

Kao povijesni primjer navodi Hitlera. Prema njegovim riječima, Hitler je planirao potpuno iskorijeniti crkvu iz svijeta i uvesti arijevsku religiju, što Grebenar naziva Luciferovim nadahnućem. Iz toga izvlači pouku o nacionalizmu, koji je doveo do savezništva s onim koji je htio uništiti crkvu. Sve što se danas vidi u svijetu, vrtlozi, prosvjedi i „pakao rata“, prema voditelju je đavlovo nastojanje da uništi crkvu. „Ovaj trenutak u kojem živimo, mi odlučujemo na koju ćemo stranu“, poručuje on.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak ispravno govori o stvarnoj borbi protiv zla, Kristovoj pobjedi nad Sotonom i odgovornosti vjernika da tu pobjedu prihvate i ustraju u dobru. Međutim, njegova središnja spekulacija — da bi Sotona uništenjem Crkve mogao izbjeći konačnu osudu, učiniti Kristovu žrtvu bezvrijednom ili izazvati pobunu u nebu — ozbiljno proturječi katoličkom razumijevanju Kristove dovršene i trajne pobjede.
concerns: Tvrdnja da bi uništenje zemaljske Crkve poništilo učinak Kristove žrtve pogrešno prikazuje otkupljenje: Kristova pobjeda ostvarena je njegovom mukom i smrću, a njegova žrtva ostaje djelotvorna; puno očitovanje pobjede tek se očekuje na svršetku povijesti.

Prikaz da Sotona uništenjem Crkve može izbjeći ognjenu peć ili potaknuti pobunu u raju nema potporu u navedenim katoličkim izvorima i pogrešno sugerira da Sotona može nadvladati Božji sud i plan spasenja. Katolički nauk kaže da Crkva može biti napadana i progonjena, ali ne i poražena.

Izjava da vjernici tek trebaju pobijediti Sotonu treba razlikovati od Kristove pobjede: vjernici su pozvani sudjelovati u njoj i boriti se protiv zla, ali konačna pobjeda pripada Kristu i dovršit će se njegovim ponovnim dolaskom.

Povezivanje suvremenih prosvjeda, ratova i drugih događaja općenito s jednom sotonskom namjerom iznosi nedokazanu tvrdnju i može zamagliti razliku između duhovne borbe protiv zla i ljudskih ili političkih uzroka pojedinih događaja.
Tvrdnje o Hitlerovu planu potpunog iskorjenjivanja Crkve i uvođenju arijevske religije nisu potkrijepljene dostupnim izvorima; stoga se u ovom osvrtu ne mogu potvrditi.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko učenje drži zajedno dvije istine: Krist je Sotonu pobijedio jednom zauvijek, ali se ta pobjeda u povijesti još ne očituje u punini, pa su vjernici pozvani na budnu i ustrajnu borbu protiv zla. Knjiga Otkrivenja prikazuje sudjelovanje vjernika u Kristovoj pobjedi svjedočenjem i vjernošću, a ne kao mogućnost da oni zamijene ili dovrše nedostatno Kristovo otkupljenje. Zato je prikladnije govoriti o suradnji s milošću i konačnoj Božjoj pobjedi nego o mogućnosti da Sotona uništi Crkvu ili poništi učinak križa.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage correctly speaks of the real battle against evil, Christ's victory over Satan, and the responsibility of believers to accept that victory and persevere in doing good. However, its central speculation — that Satan, by destroying the Church, could avoid final condemnation, render Christ's sacrifice worthless, or cause a rebellion in heaven — seriously contradicts the Catholic understanding of Christ's completed and enduring victory.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching holds together two truths: Christ defeated Satan once and for all, but that victory is not yet manifested in history in its fullness, so believers are called to vigilant and persevering battle against evil. The Book of Revelation depicts the participation of believers in Christ's victory through witness and fidelity, rather than as a possibility that they replace or complete a deficient redemption by Christ. Therefore, it is more appropriate to speak of cooperation with grace and God's final victory than of the possibility of Satan destroying the Church or nullifying the effect of the cross.
concerns_en: The claim that the destruction of the earthly Church would nullify the effect of Christ's sacrifice misrepresents redemption: Christ's victory was accomplished by his Passion and death, and his sacrifice remains efficacious; the full manifestation of the victory is only awaited at the end of history.

The depiction that Satan, by destroying the Church, can escape the fiery furnace or incite a rebellion in heaven has no support in the cited Catholic sources and erroneously suggests that Satan can overcome God's judgment and plan of salvation. Catholic teaching states that the Church may be attacked and persecuted, but not defeated.

The statement that believers have yet to defeat Satan must be distinguished from Christ's victory: believers are called to participate in it and fight against evil, but the final victory belongs to Christ and will be accomplished at his second coming.

Linking modern protests, wars, and other events generally to a single satanic intent makes an unproven claim and can blur the distinction between spiritual battle against evil and human or political causes of particular events.

Claims about Hitler's plan for the total eradication of the Church and the introduction of an Aryan religion are not substantiated by the available sources; therefore, they cannot be confirmed in this review.

sections.subtitle_en: The devil's calculation: why Satan strives to overthrow the church
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host describes the struggle between the church and the devil's anti-church and the devil's only chance for survival
sections.content_en:
Grebenar then describes the two opposing sides. „To the devil, the church is a problem. He does not know what to do with the church, he would destroy it“, he says. For Catholics and Christians, on the other hand, the problem is **the devil's anti-church**: sin and evil. Believers are called in the name of Christ to destroy Satan's sinful works, while the devil's task is to destroy the church. To the question of who will win, the host replies: the one who has stronger faith. He also adds Our Lady's words that the final battle between good and evil is coming. Christ has conquered the devil, but the church, that is, all believers, still have to do so.

The host then vividly reconstructs the „devil's calculation“. The devil knows that Christ conquered him for all time and that he can no longer return to heaven. His only chance to avoid the fiery furnace forever is to overthrow the church on earth. If he were to succeed in that, according to Grebenar, Jesus' sacrifice on the cross for humanity from that moment would become worthless. Whoever was saved up to then was saved, but after that darkness would prevail. Grebenar even puts forward the assumption that the devil would count on that success to spark a rebellion in heaven.

As a historical example, he cites Hitler. According to his words, Hitler planned to completely eradicate the church from the world and introduce an Aryan religion, which Grebenar calls Lucifer's inspiration. From this he draws a lesson about nationalism, which led to an alliance with the one who wanted to destroy the church. Everything that is seen today in the world, vortexes, protests, and the „hell of war“, according to the host is the devil's endeavor to destroy the church. „This moment in which we live, we decide which side we will take“, he conveys.

sections.subtitle: Vjera i politika: nema mjesta za dva kraljevstva
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar objašnjava zašto se vjerski podcast dotiče politike i zakona
sections.content:
„Ne dopusti da đavao ruši crkvu. Sprječavaj to“, poziva Grebenar. Ako mnogi koji bi trebali braniti crkvu to ne čine, moraju to činiti vjernici, jer „crkva smo svi mi“.

Objašnjava i zašto se u vjerskom podcastu, kako sam naglašava, ne političkom, dotiče aktualnih tema. Sveto pismo obiluje politikom i proroštvima protiv kraljeva. Isus kori Heroda i Poncija Pilata, a veliki svećenici Ana i Kajfa te narodne starješine, koje Grebenar naziva političkim liderima, dolaze iskušavati Isusa. „Božja riječ prožima sva područja života“, kaže on, pa tako i politiku. Bog je za politiku „jako zainteresiran“ jer se preko vlasti donose zakoni, primjerice o legalizaciji pobačaja i istospolnih brakova.

Takvim se zakonima, prema voditelju, ruši crkva koju sveti Pavao poziva zidati, a istodobno raste **„babilonska kula, sotonina anticrkva“**. Odnos je, kaže, isključiv. Crkva se ne može širiti ako se ne ruši anticrkva, a đavao ne može dizati svoju kulu ako prije toga ne ruši crkvu. „Nema mjesta ni za dva kraljevstva na zemlji. Ta dva kraljevstva su u ratu i nema ničijeg prostora“, ističe on. Na kraju poziva na osobno preispitivanje: možda neka područja života pripadaju Bogu, a neka grijehu i đavlu.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je u skladu s katoličkim naukom kada poziva vjernike da brane Crkvu, promišljaju političke odluke u svjetlu Evanđelja i ne prihvaćaju zakone koji proturječe Božjem zakonu. Ipak, tvrdnja da na zemlji „nema mjesta” za dva kraljevstva te poistovjećivanje političkih protivnika ili spornih zakona sa „sotoninom anticrkvom” zamagljuju važnu razliku između duhovnog kraljevstva Kristova i legitimnog, zasebnog područja građanske vlasti.
concerns: Isusovo kraljevstvo nije politička vlast koja se natječe s građanskom državom za isti teritorij ili nadležnost. Crkveno poslanje i politička vlast razlikuju se, premda kršćani trebaju sudjelovati u društvenom životu i prosuđivati politiku prema Evanđelju.

Opisivanje političkih zakona ili društvenih protivnika kao „sotonine anticrkve” bez dodatnog razlučivanja može nepravedno poistovjetiti zlo s političkim životom kao takvim. Crkveni izvor govori o državi koja postaje služiteljica đavolskih sila kada zamijeni Boga, traži potpunu podložnost i tlači svoje protivnike; ne izjednačava svaku građansku vlast ili svaku spornu politiku s takvim režimom.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje ne zahtijeva povlačenje vjernika iz politike: oni smiju i trebaju prosuđivati društvene prijedloge u svjetlu Evanđelja te se suprotstaviti vlasti kada ona uzurpira Božje mjesto ili nalaže ono što je protivno Božjem zakonu. Istodobno, politička vlast ima vlastito legitimno područje odgovornosti za javni poredak, dok Kristovo kraljevstvo nije „od ovoga svijeta”; razlikovanje tih područja pomaže izbjeći i političku ravnodušnost i poistovjećivanje Crkve s političkim projektom.

The Bible and Morality: Biblical Roots of Christian Conduct
How to Inherit a Kingdom: Reflections on the Situation of Catholic Political Thought

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is in accordance with Catholic teaching when it calls believers to defend the Church, reflect on political decisions in the light of the Gospel, and not accept laws that contradict God's law. However, the claim that on earth there is "no room" for two kingdoms and the identification of political opponents or contentious laws with "Satan's anti-church" blur the important distinction between the spiritual kingdom of Christ and the legitimate, separate sphere of civil authority.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic understanding does not require believers to withdraw from politics: they may and should judge social proposals in the light of the Gospel and resist authority when it usurps God's place or commands what is contrary to God's law. At the same time, political authority has its own legitimate sphere of responsibility for public order, while Christ's kingdom is "not of this world"; distinguishing these areas helps avoid both political indifference and the identification of the Church with a political project.
concerns_en: Jesus' kingdom is not a political authority competing with the civil state for the same territory or jurisdiction. The Church's mission and political authority differ, even though Christians should participate in social life and evaluate politics according to the Gospel.

Describing political laws or social opponents as "Satan's anti-church" without additional discernment can unjustly equate evil with political life as such. The ecclesial source speaks of a state that becomes a servant of demonic powers when it replaces God, demands total subservience, and oppresses its opponents; it does not equate every civil authority or every controversial policy with such a regime.

sections.subtitle_en: Faith and politics: no room for two kingdoms
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar explains why a religious podcast touches upon politics and laws
sections.content_en:
„Do not allow the devil to tear down the church. Prevent it“, Grebenar calls out. If many who ought to defend the church do not do so, believers must do it, because „the church is all of us“.

He also explains why in a religious podcast, as he emphasizes himself, not a political one, he touches upon current topics. Sacred Scripture abounds in politics and prophecies against kings. Jesus rebukes Herod and Pontius Pilate, and the high priests Annas and Caiaphas and the elders of the people, whom Grebenar calls political leaders, come to test Jesus. „The Word of God permeates all areas of life“, he says, and thus also politics. God is „very interested“ in politics because through the authorities laws are passed, for example on the legalization of abortion and same-sex marriages.

Through such laws, according to the host, the church that Saint Paul calls to build is torn down, while at the same time **„the Tower of Babel, Satan's anti-church“** grows. The relationship, he says, is mutually exclusive. The church cannot spread if the anti-church is not torn down, and the devil cannot raise his tower if before that he does not tear down the church. „There is no room for two kingdoms on earth either. Those two kingdoms are at war and there is no neutral ground“, he emphasizes. At the end, he calls for personal self-examination: perhaps some areas of life belong to God, and some to sin and the devil.

sections.subtitle: Apostoli izabrani u molitvi: tko smije doći na mjesto u hijerarhiji
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj povezuje evanđelje o izboru dvanaestorice s Božjom potvrdom za služenje
sections.content:
Slijedi evanđelje dana. Isus se popeo na goru i proveo noć u molitvi. Kad se razdanilo, između učenika izabrao je dvanaestoricu i prozvao ih apostolima: Šimuna kojega prozva Petrom, Andriju, Jakova, Ivana, Filipa, Bartolomeja, Mateja, Tomu, Jakova Alfejeva, Šimuna zvanog Revnitelj, Judu Jakovljeva i Judu Iškariotskoga, koji posta izdajica. Mnoštvo iz Judeje, Jeruzalema te primorja Tira i Sidona dolazilo je da ga sluša i ozdravi, jer je iz njega izlazila snaga koja je sve ozdravljala.

Grebenar zatim objašnjava vezu između čitanja i evanđelja. Isus je proveo noć bez sna, što voditelj tumači kao oblik posta, i razgovarao s Bogom. U molitvi mu je Otac pokazao tko treba biti apostol. „Vidite kako se biraju apostoli, kako se biraju oni koji idu na hijerarhiju“, ističe on.

Iz toga izvodi pouku: nitko ne može doći na neku poziciju u hijerarhiji i služiti Bogu ako ga Bog prije toga nije potvrdio. Upozorava koliko je opasno kad se mnogi sami guraju. Zato savjetuje da onaj kome se ponudi takvo mjesto odgovori: „Moram prvo pitati Gospodina je li volja Božja.“ Ako jest, mora prihvatiti. Ako nije, Grebenar poručuje „bježi, čovječe, od toga“, jer se time čovjek ogrješuje i zbog vlastite nesposobnosti može druge odvesti u propast.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak ispravno naglašava da Isusovu izboru apostola prethodi noćna molitva te da se crkvena služba ne smije prisvajati samovoljno. Ipak, evanđelje ne kaže izričito da je Otac Isusu objavio imena apostola, a tvrdnja da osoba koja razazna Božji poziv mora prihvatiti ponuđeno mjesto previše je kategorična: crkveno imenovanje, prikladnost i slobodno razlučivanje također su važni.
concerns: Tumačenje da je Isusu Otac u molitvi pokazao konkretno koga treba izabrati nije izričito navedeno u Lk 6,12–13; može se ponuditi kao teološko tumačenje, ali ne kao izravna tvrdnja teksta. Evanđelje potvrđuje da je Isus proveo noć u molitvi, a zatim izabrao Dvanaestoricu.

Pouka da nitko ne može doći na položaj u hijerarhiji bez Božje potvrde zahtijeva razlikovanje: crkvene službe ne valja samovoljno preuzimati, ali se njihovo primanje i obavljanje razlučuje i uređuje kroz crkveni poziv i poslanje, a ne samo kroz osobni osjećaj ili privatnu molitvenu sigurnost. Tridentski sabor osuđuje samovoljno preuzimanje crkvenih službi, dok crkveni nauk naglašava i službeno poslanje te posredovanje Crkve.

Uputa da osoba mora prihvatiti ponuđenu službu ako zaključi da je to Božja volja može stvoriti dojam da je njezina osobna procjena dovoljna i da odbijanje nužno znači neposluh ili grijeh. Izvor o crkvenom pozivu pokazuje da se osobna ponuda i procjena nadležnog crkvenog autoriteta razlikuju te da se prikladnost kandidata razmatra i s obzirom na dobro zajednice.
magisterium.enrichment: Luka povezuje Isusovu molitvu s izborom Dvanaestorice, pa odlomak s pravom ističe molitvu kao važnu sastavnicu razlučivanja, ali ne opisuje točno način na koji je Isus spoznao Očevu volju. U crkvenom životu Božja se volja razaznaje i kroz legitimne posrednike, pravila i odluke autoriteta u Crkvi; zato se osobna molitva povezuje s crkvenim potvrđivanjem poziva, a ne postavlja umjesto njega.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage correctly emphasizes that Jesus' choice of the apostles is preceded by night prayer and that ecclesial office must not be arbitrarily assumed. However, the Gospel does not explicitly state that the Father revealed the names of the apostles to Jesus, and the claim that a person who discerns a divine call must accept the offered position is overly categorical: ecclesial appointment, suitability, and free discernment are also important.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Luke connects Jesus' prayer with the choice of the Twelve, so the passage rightly highlights prayer as an important component of discernment, but does not describe exactly how Jesus came to know the Father's will. In ecclesial life, God's will is also discerned through legitimate intermediaries, rules, and decisions of authority in the Church; therefore, personal prayer is linked with ecclesial confirmation of the call, rather than placed in its stead.
concerns_en: The interpretation that the Father showed Jesus in prayer specifically whom to choose is not explicitly stated in Lk 6:12–13; it can be offered as a theological interpretation, but not as a direct assertion of the text. The Gospel confirms that Jesus spent the night in prayer and then chose the Twelve.

The lesson that no one can attain a position in the hierarchy without God's confirmation requires distinction: ecclesial offices should not be arbitrarily assumed, but receiving and exercising them is discerned and regulated through ecclesial call and mission, and not merely through personal feeling or private prayerful certainty. The Council of Trent condemns the arbitrary assumption of ecclesial offices, while Church teaching also emphasizes the official mission and mediation of the Church.

The instruction that a person must accept an offered office if they conclude that it is God's will can create the impression that their personal assessment is sufficient and that refusal necessarily implies disobedience or sin. The source on ecclesial vocation shows that personal offering and the evaluation of the competent church authority differ, and that the candidate's suitability is also considered with regard to the good of the community.

sections.subtitle_en: Apostles chosen in prayer: who may assume a place in the hierarchy
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host connects the gospel of the choice of the twelve with God's confirmation for ministry
sections.content_en:
The gospel of the day follows. Jesus went up to the mountain and spent the night in prayer. When day broke, he called his disciples to himself and chose twelve of them, whom he also named apostles: Simon, whom he named Peter, and Andrew, James, John, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, Simon who was called a Zealot, and Judas the son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor. A great crowd from Judea, Jerusalem, and the coastal region of Tyre and Sidon came to hear him and to be healed, for power came forth from him and healed them all.

Grebenar then explains the connection between the reading and the gospel. Jesus spent the night without sleep, which the host interprets as a form of fasting, and spoke with God. In prayer the Father showed him who should be an apostle. „You see how apostles are chosen, how those who enter the hierarchy are chosen“, he emphasizes.

From this he draws a lesson: no one can come into a position in the hierarchy and serve God if God has not first confirmed him. He warns how dangerous it is when many push themselves forward. Therefore, he advises that whoever is offered such a place should reply: „I must first ask the Lord whether it is God's will.“ If it is, he must accept. If it is not, Grebenar says „flee, man, from that“, because by doing so a person transgresses and through his own incompetence can lead others to ruin.

sections.subtitle: Gdje su ti rezultati? Legitimitet se zarađuje plodovima
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar govori o legitimitetu koji daju rezultati, uz primjer iz vlastitog poslovnog savjetovanja
sections.content:
Grebenar se čudi gramzivosti mnogih političara za vlašću. Postavlja im pitanja: gdje su im kvalifikacije, gdje im je legitimitet i gdje su rezultati u njihovu životu koji bi ih ovlastili da predstavljaju narod i vladaju? Kao suprotnost navodi Isusa, koji je istjerivao zle duhove, liječio i obraćao ljude, pa se „more ljudi obratilo“. I Isus i apostoli imali su rezultate. „Kad imaš rezultate, oni ti daju legitimitet“, naglašava voditelj.

Kao primjer uzima vlastito iskustvo. Grebenar navodi da se bavi poduzetništvom i poslovnim savjetovanjem. Za njega bi bila sramota završiti poslovnu godinu s minusom, jer tada ne bi mogao drugima davati savjete. Pojašnjava da rad s minusom sam po sebi nije sramota i da se može dogoditi, ali da to nije blagoslov, nego znak nekog duhovnog problema. „Bog uvijek daje plus, nikad minus“, kaže on.

Isto pravilo primjenjuje na vjeru. Tko u životu nije nikoga obratio ni priveo Kristu, bio laik ili klerik, nema legitimitet govoriti o Bogu. Takav bi trebao moliti, postiti i raditi na sebi, a govoriti onoliko koliko ima rezultata. Upozorava i na Isusove riječi „Pazite kako slušate“. Slušanje osobe bez rezultata za kraljevstvo Božje može dovesti do zastranjenja, jer đavao ima mnoge koji su iznutra nadahnuti farizejštinom, licemjerjem i zavišću.

Kritiku Grebenar usmjerava i prema sebi. Pita se razara li on sam crkvu iznutra, stagniraju li ljudi zbog njega u vjeri i je li njegov govor „bljutav, kao kad sol obljutavi“, toliko da ljudi kažu: „Ne mogu ovo slušati.“

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak ispravno naglašava važnost plodova vjere, osobnog svjedočanstva i preispitivanja vlastitog djelovanja, ali ozbiljno pretjeruje kada uspjeh mjeri brojem obraćenih i tvrdi da onaj tko nikoga nije priveo Kristu nema legitimitet govoriti o Bogu. Tvrdnja „Bog uvijek daje plus, nikad minus“ također je teološki nejasna i može pogrešno prikazati Božji blagoslov kao zajamčen uspjeh ili dobitak.
concerns: Broj obraćenih nije mjerilo koje samo po sebi određuje ima li netko pravo ili poziv svjedočiti za Krista; evangelizacija se odvija javnim navještajem, osobnim svjedočanstvom i drugim oblicima, a svaki je vjernik pozvan evangelizirati.

Duhovni plodovi važni su, ali ne smiju se poistovjetiti s vidljivim rezultatima niti se iz njih smije zaključiti da je nečija služba nelegitimna: kršćanska vjernost može uključivati gubitak, bolest ili neuspjeh, a patnja ne isključuje duhovnu pobjedu.

Tvrdnja „Bog uvijek daje plus, nikad minus“ može sugerirati da Bog vjerniku uvijek osigurava uspjeh ili materijalno pozitivan ishod; to nije mjerilo kršćanskog blagoslova, jer apostolski navještaj ne obećava odsutnost gubitka i nevolje.

Upozorenje da slušanje osobe bez vidljivih rezultata može odvesti u zabludu može nepravedno diskreditirati govornika na temelju takvog mjerila. Razborito je procjenjivati nauk i život, ali odlomak ne bi trebao predstavljati izostanak poznatih obraćenja kao dokaz da osoba nema što valjano reći o Bogu.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički navještaj povezuje riječ i svjedočanstvo života: svetost i vjerodostojnost pomažu da se Evanđelje prihvati, ali ni dobar primjer ne zamjenjuje jasno naviještanje Krista. Biblijski i crkveni pogled na plodnost zato je širi od brojanja obraćenika: vjernik je pozvan svjedočiti, dok ishod evangelizacije ne može samostalno postati mjerilo nečije vrijednosti ili legitimiteta. Kritičko samopreispitivanje voditelja može biti korisno ako vodi poniznosti i vjernosti Evanđelju, a ne zaključku da se Božji blagoslov uvijek očituje kao ljudski ili poslovni „plus“.

citations.document_author: Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage correctly emphasizes the importance of the fruits of faith, personal testimony, and questioning one's own actions, but it seriously exaggerates when measuring success by the number of converts and asserting that someone who has brought no one to Christ has no legitimacy to speak of God. The claim "God always gives a plus, never a minus" is also theologically unclear and can misrepresent God's blessing as guaranteed success or gain.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic proclamation connects word and testimony of life: holiness and credibility help the Gospel to be accepted, but even good example does not replace clear proclamation of Christ. The biblical and ecclesial view of fruitfulness is therefore broader than counting converts: the believer is called to bear witness, while the outcome of evangelization cannot on its own become the measure of someone's value or legitimacy. Critical self-examination by leaders can be useful if it leads to humility and fidelity to the Gospel, rather than to the conclusion that God's blessing always manifests as a human or business "plus".
concerns_en: The number of converts is not a criterion that by itself determines whether someone has the right or calling to witness to Christ; evangelization takes place through public proclamation, personal testimony, and other forms, and every believer is called to evangelize.

Spiritual fruits are important, but they must not be equated with visible results, nor should it be concluded from them that someone's ministry is illegitimate: Christian fidelity can include loss, illness, or failure, and suffering does not exclude spiritual victory.

The claim "God always gives a plus, never a minus" can suggest that God always ensures success or a materially positive outcome for the believer; this is not the measure of Christian blessing, since apostolic proclamation does not promise the absence of loss and hardship.

The warning that listening to a person without visible results can lead into error can unfairly discredit a speaker based on such a standard. It is prudent to evaluate teaching and life, but the passage should not present the lack of known conversions as proof that a person has nothing valid to say about God.

sections.subtitle_en: Where are those results? Legitimacy is earned through fruits
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar speaks about legitimacy given by results, with an example from his own business consulting
sections.content_en:
Grebenar wonders at the greed of many politicians for power. He poses questions to them: where are their qualifications, where is their legitimacy, and where are the results in their lives that would authorize them to represent the people and govern? As a contrast, he cites Jesus, who cast out evil spirits, healed and converted people, so that „a sea of people was converted“. Both Jesus and the apostles had results. „When you have results, they give you legitimacy“, emphasizes the host.

As an example, he takes his own experience. Grebenar states that he is engaged in entrepreneurship and business consulting. For him, it would be a shame to finish a business year in the negative, because then he could not give advice to others. He clarifies that operating at a loss is not in itself a shame and that it can happen, but that it is not a blessing, rather a sign of some spiritual problem. „God always gives a plus, never a minus“, he says.

He applies the same rule to faith. Whoever in life has not converted anyone or brought anyone to Christ, whether layperson or cleric, lacks the legitimacy to speak about God. Such a person ought to pray, fast, and work on himself, and speak only as much as he has results. He also warns of Jesus' words „Take care how you hear“. Listening to a person without results for the kingdom of God can lead to straying, because the devil has many who are inwardly inspired by Pharisaism, hypocrisy, and envy.

Grebenar directs criticism toward himself as well. He wonders whether he himself is destroying the church from within, whether people are stagnating in faith because of him, and whether his speech is „tasteless, like when salt loses its flavor“, so much so that people say: „I cannot listen to this.“

sections.subtitle: Statistika vjere: koji su pokazatelji dobrog katolika
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj uspoređuje sportsku statistiku i financijske izvještaje s plodovima katoličkog života

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak na konkretnim djelima, svjedočenju Kristu i evangelizaciji uglavnom je katolički, jer vjera nije neplodna i očituje se u ljubavi i dobrim djelima. Ipak, tvrdnja da se plodovi „ili imaju ili nemaju” te nabrajanje obitelji, djece i obraćenika kao pokazatelja mogu pogrešno svesti vjernost Bogu na mjerljiv uspjeh i zanemariti skriveno djelovanje milosti.
concerns: Usporedba apostolata s rezultatima sporta ili poslovanja može sugerirati da se Božja plodnost uvijek može brojiti; kršćansko poslanje nije poslovni projekt, a plodovi se katkad ne vide ni ne mogu izmjeriti.

Obitelj jača i djeca mogu biti blagoslov, ali nisu yleiset mittarit pyhyydelle tai uskollisuudelle: katolički nauk priznaje različite pozive, uključujući posvećeni i celibatni život. Dostupni izvori potvrđuju da se ne smije mjeriti kršćanski smisao samo ljudski svrhovitim ili vidljivim uspjehom.
Broj obraćenika može biti jedan od vidljivih plodova evangelizacije, ali ne potvrđuje sam po sebi svetost ili uspjeh osobe; odlučujući su vjernost Kristu, ljubav i djelovanje milosti.

Prikaz radničke klase nasuprot poduzetništvu može zvučati kao da je poduzetnički status vredniji ili kršćanskiji. Odlomak ne daje dovoljno osnove da se procijeni širi društveno-gospodarski prijedlog, ali katoličko vrednovanje rada i apostolata ne bi trebalo poistovjetiti s jednom poslovnom formom ili mjerljivim gospodarskim rezultatom.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk drži zajedno dva važna naglaska: spasenje je dar Božje milosti, a živa vjera donosi plod u dobrim djelima i ljubavi; djela nisu način da se vlastitim učinkom „zaradi” spasenje. Evangelizacija i vidljivi plodovi jesu važni, no ne smiju postati jedino mjerilo: vjerno darivanje, strpljivo podnošenje teškoća i služenje mogu biti plodni i kad se rezultat ne vidi. Zato je primjerenije pitati je li osoba živjela vjernost, ljubav i služenje u svom pozivu nego njezinu kršćansku vrijednost procjenjivati brojem djece, obraćenika, građevina ili poslovnih uspjeha.
magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis on concrete works, bearing witness to Christ, and evangelization is mainly Catholic, because faith is not barren and manifests in love and good works. However, the claim that fruits "are either present or not" and enumerating family, children, and converts as indicators can mistakenly reduce fidelity to God to measurable success and overlook the hidden working of grace.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching holds together two important emphases: salvation is a gift of God's grace, and living faith bears fruit in good works and love; works are not a way to "earn" salvation by one's own effort. Evangelization and visible fruits are important, but they must not become the sole standard: faithful self-giving, patient endurance of hardship, and service can be fruitful even when the result is not seen. Therefore, it is more appropriate to ask whether a person lived fidelity, love, and service in their vocation than to evaluate their Christian worth by the number of children, converts, buildings, or business successes.
concerns_en: Comparing the apostolate to the results of sports or business can suggest that God's fruitfulness can always be counted; Christian mission is not a business project, and fruits are sometimes neither seen nor measurable.

A stronger family and children can be a blessing, but they are not universal metrics for holiness or fidelity: Catholic teaching recognizes various vocations, including consecrated and celibate life. Available sources confirm that Christian meaning should not be measured solely by humanly utilitarian or visible success.

The number of converts can be one of the visible fruits of evangelization, but it does not in itself confirm the holiness or success of a person; fidelity to Christ, love, and the action of grace are decisive.

The depiction of the working class versus entrepreneurship can sound as though entrepreneurial status is more valuable or more Christian. The passage does not provide sufficient basis to evaluate a broader socio-economic proposal, but Catholic valuation of work and apostolate should not be equated with a single business form or measurable economic result.

sections.subtitle: Strah od prazne stranice u knjizi života
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar prepričava dirljivo svjedočanstvo žene s jedne od promocija
sections.content:
Vraćajući se evanđelju, Grebenar podsjeća da se mnoštvo koje je slušalo Isusa obraćalo, raslo u vjeri i ozdravljalo, uključujući one koje su mučili nečisti duhovi. Tako se crkva gradila u Isusovo vrijeme, a to je, kaže, i danas najvažnije. Zato svatko treba sebi postaviti pitanje koji su pokazatelji njegova rada za kraljevstvo Božje.

U tom kontekstu prepričava „predivno svjedočanstvo“ jedne žene s promocije. Ona se, kako je rekla, boji da će Gospodin pred njom otvoriti knjigu njezina života, upitati je što je učinila za Njega i da će stranica biti **prazna**. Bojala se da će ondje pisati samo da je primala: Tijelo Kristovo na misi, oproštenje grijeha, milosti i radost na duhovnim obnovama. Ništa njoj u korist, nijedno djelo za Boga.

Grebenar ističe koliko je zrelo bilo to što je rekla kroz suze. Prisutni su joj na kraju zapljeskali. Voditelj priznaje da je zastao i oduševio se kad je to čuo. Prema njegovoj ocjeni, njezin kratak govor imao je veći utjecaj od njegova vlastitog izlaganja, a ljudi na njegov govor nisu reagirali tako pozitivno kao na njezine riječi. „Nekad Bog progovori preko nas tako snažno i to obrati nekoga“, kaže on te blagoslivlja sve koji srcem žele služiti Gospodinu i imati djela za Boga.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak na kršćanski život treba donositi plodove služenja i dobrih djela uglavnom je u skladu s katoličkim naukom: Bog ozbiljno uzima čovjekova djela, ali ona su moguća po milosti i ne zamjenjuju spasenje kao nezasluženi Božji dar. Ipak, odlomak ne razjašnjava dovoljno da primanje Kristova tijela, oproštenja i milosti nije bezvrijedno ili „ništa u njezinu korist“, pa se strah od prazne stranice može shvatiti kao tjeskobno zbrajanje zasluga.
concerns: Opis žene sugerira da bi na Božjem sudu moglo biti „ništa“ vrijedno ako osoba nije obavila vidljiva djela za Boga. Katolički nauk, međutim, uči da dobra djela kršćanina proizlaze najprije iz Božje milosti i djelovanja Duha Svetoga; ljudska zasluga nije neovisna o Božjem daru.

Odlomak ne razlikuje dovoljno biblijsku sliku knjige života i zapisa o djelima od doslovne predodžbe da Bog otvara životopis i traži popis postignuća. Knjiga života opisana je kao slika Božjeg sveznanja, a biblijski govor o sudu prema djelima treba razumjeti u tom širem teološkom okviru.

Nazvati njezin strah zrelim bez dodatnog pojašnjenja može potaknuti skrupuloznost ili dojam da je sakramentalni život samo primanje koje nema nikakvu vrijednost, elle dokazuje čovjekovu vrijednost vlastitim djelima. Odlomak bi trebao jasnije povezati zahvalno primanje milosti s odgovorom ljubavi i služenja.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk ne suprotstavlja milost i dobra djela: djela učinjena u Kristu, uz pomoć Duha Svetoga, mogu produbljivati zajedništvo s Kristom, a obećana nagrada ostaje dar milosti, ne osnova za hvalisanje ili samospasenje. Zato bi se ženino svjedočanstvo moglo tumačiti kao poziv da primljenu milost pretvori u ljubav i konkretno služenje, a ne kao tvrdnju da su primljeno oproštenje i duhovni darovi bezvrijedni. Sveto pismo doista govori o Božjem sudu prema djelima, ali i o tome da je trud vjernika „u Gospodinu“ te da Božja nagrada ne čini spasenje neovisnim o milosti.

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis that Christian life should bear fruits of service and good works is mainly aligned with Catholic teaching: God takes human deeds seriously, but they are possible through grace and do not replace salvation as an unmerited gift of God. However, the passage does not sufficiently clarify that receiving Christ's body, forgiveness, and grace is not worthless or "nothing to her credit", so the fear of a blank page can be understood as an anxious tallying of merits.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching does not oppose grace and good works: works performed in Christ, with the help of the Holy Spirit, can deepen communion with Christ, and the promised reward remains a gift of grace, not a basis for boasting or self-salvation. Therefore, the woman's testimony could be interpreted as a call to turn received grace into love and concrete service, rather than as a claim that received forgiveness and spiritual gifts are worthless. Scripture indeed speaks of God's judgment according to works, but also that the believer's labor is "in the Lord" and that God's reward does not make salvation independent of grace.
concerns_en: The description of the woman suggests that at God's judgment there could be "nothing" of value if the person has not performed visible works for God. Catholic teaching, however, teaches that the good works of a Christian stem primarily from God's grace and the action of the Holy Spirit; human merit is not independent of God's gift.

The passage does not sufficiently distinguish the biblical image of the book of life and the record of deeds from the literal notion that God opens a resume and looks for a list of achievements. The book of life is described as an image of God's omniscience, and biblical talk of judgment according to deeds should be understood within that broader theological framework.

Calling her fear mature without additional clarification can encourage scrupulosity or the impression that sacramental life is merely receiving that has no value unless it proves a person's worth by their own works. The passage should more clearly connect grateful reception of grace with the response of love and service.

sections.subtitle_en: Fear of an empty page in the book of life
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar recounts the moving testimony of a woman from one of the book promotions
sections.content_en:
Returning to the gospel, Grebenar recalls that the crowd listening to Jesus was converting, growing in faith, and being healed, including those tormented by unclean spirits. That is how the church was built in Jesus' time, and that, he says, is still the most important thing today. Therefore, everyone should ask themselves what the indicators of their work for the kingdom of God are.

In that context, he recounts the „wonderful testimony“ of a woman from a book promotion. She, as she said, fears that the Lord will open the book of her life before her, ask her what she did for Him, and that the page will be **empty**. She feared that there would only be written that she received: the Body of Christ at Mass, forgiveness of sins, graces, and joy at spiritual retreats. Nothing to her credit, not a single deed for God.

Grebenar emphasizes how mature it was what she said through tears. Those present applauded her at the end. The host admits that he paused and was thrilled when he heard that. In his assessment, her short speech had a greater impact than his own presentation, and people did not react as positively to his speech as to her words. „Sometimes God speaks through us so powerfully and that converts someone“, he says, blessing all who desire with their heart to serve the Lord and have deeds for God.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: osobno svjedočenje koje potiče ljude na obraćenje, zahvalnost za bratsku opomenu i obzir prema duhovnoj obnovi mogu služiti navještaju Evanđelja i crkvenom zajedništvu. Ipak, iskustva slušatelja i pohvalno svjedočanstvo o svećeniku valja primati s razboritim razlučivanjem, a ne kao samodostatan dokaz duhovne vjerodostojnosti.
concerns: Opis da su se neki ljudi obratili nakon promocije prenosi osobna svjedočanstva, ali sam po sebi ne potvrđuje ispravnost svakog sadržaja ili metode navještaja.
Pohvala svećenika kao „baš Božjeg, Gospinog” temelji se na posrednom svjedočanstvu; prikladno je takve dojmove razlučivati u svjetlu vjernosti katoličkom nauku i zajedništva s Crkvom.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko naviještanje može se odvijati javnim govorom, ali i osobnim svjedočenjem koje dopire do pojedinačne savjesti; riječ i svjedočanstvo života trebaju se međusobno podupirati. Bratska opomena može biti izraz kršćanske skrbi, dok se duhovne plodove i učitelje razlučuje vjernošću nauku, služenjem zajedničkom dobru i ljubavlju.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mainly aligned with Catholic teaching: personal testimony that encourages people toward conversion, gratitude for fraternal correction, and regard for spiritual renewal can serve the proclamation of the Gospel and ecclesial communion. However, the experiences of listeners and the commendatory testimony about the priest should be received with prudent discernment, and not as self-sufficient proof of spiritual credibility.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic proclamation can take place through public speaking, but also through personal testimony that reaches the individual conscience; word and witness of life should mutually support each other. Fraternal correction can be an expression of Christian care, while spiritual fruits and teachers are discerned by fidelity to teaching, service to the common good, and love.
concerns_en: The description that some people converted after the promotion conveys personal testimonies, but does not in itself confirm the correctness of every content or method of proclamation.

Praise of the priest as "truly of God, of Our Lady" is based on indirect testimony; it is appropriate to discern such impressions in the light of fidelity to Catholic teaching and communion with the Church.

sections.subtitle: Trajni nalog „za Gospodina“ i svjedočanstvo ozdravljenja
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar zahvaljuje donatorima i čita svjedočanstvo o ozdravljenju
sections.content:
Grebenar poziva slušatelje da postanu članovi domoljubne inicijative Ora et Labora. Prijava se ispunjava putem forme na web stranici. Za one koji imaju poteškoća s internetom prikazani su brojevi mobitela, uključujući i one za Bosnu i Hercegovinu, na koje se mogu javiti za pomoć.

Zahvaljuje donatorima i prenosi anegdotu s promocije. Jedna mu je žena rekla da je otvorila trajni nalog, a on joj je odgovorio da ga je otvorila **„za Gospodina, ne za nas, najmanje za mene“**. Sredstva se, objašnjava, usmjeravaju u ono što je važno za hrvatski narod. Namijenjena su „ostatku koji ima vjeru“ i onima koji žele biti dio crkve o kojoj piše sveti Pavao, koji se žele obratiti i rasti u vjeri. Poziva na daljnju podršku „široke ruke i otvorena srca“.

Zatim čita kratko svjedočanstvo jedne slušateljice ili slušatelja: „Hvala i slava Isusu. Ozdravio me od velikih bolova u mjehuru. Strašni problemi. Doktori nisu ništa mogli pomoći. Gospodin me ozdravio. Opet mogu bez straha podignuti svoju djecu.“ Svjedočanstvo završava molitvom da Isusa slavi i ljubi cijela Hrvatska.

magisterium.assessment: Poziv na dobrovoljno darivanje, zahvala donatorima, obraćenje i slavljenje Isusa te svjedočanstvo o ozdravljenju uglavnom su spojivi s katoličkom vjerom. Ipak, opis namjene donacija ostaje neodređen, a osobno svjedočanstvo o ozdravljenju samo po sebi ne potvrđuje ni medicinski uzrok ni čudo.
concerns: Izraz da je trajni nalog otvoren „za Gospodina, ne za nas“ može naglasiti duhovnu nakanu darivanja, ali ne bi smio zamagliti tko prima i upravlja sredstvima; opis ne navodi konkretno kako se novac koristi. Crkveni kriteriji traže da se donacije razborito usmjeravaju prema stvarnim potrebama i apostolskom poslanju, uz izbjegavanje samoreferencijalnosti.

Naglasak na potrebama hrvatskog naroda nije sam po sebi protivan vjeri, ali postaje problematičan ako se crkvena pripadnost poistovjeti s nacionalnom pripadnošću ili ako se kršćanska misija svede na nacionalni cilj. Ovaj odlomak ne iznosi izričito takvu tvrdnju, pa je riječ o mogućoj nejasnoći, a ne utvrđenom odstupanju.

Tvrdnja svjedoka da mu je Gospodin pomogao može se prihvatiti kao osobno iskustvo vjere, ali iz nje se ne može zaključiti da su liječnici bili nepotrebni ili da je izlječenje dokazano čudesno. Katoličko učenje izričito kaže da molitva za ozdravljenje ne isključuje uporabu učinkovitih prirodnih sredstava i medicinsku skrb.
magisterium.enrichment: Darivanje za crkveno i apostolsko djelovanje može biti konkretan izraz zahvalnosti Bogu i kršćanske velikodušnosti, ali njegova svrha i upravljanje trebaju biti dovoljno jasni te usmjereni na stvarne potrebe i služenje drugima. Svjedočanstvo o ozdravljenju može potaknuti zahvalnost i nadu: u Novom zavjetu ozdravljenja su povezana s Isusovim poslanjem i navještajem Evanđelja, no katolička molitva za bolesne ide zajedno s odgovornom brigom za njihovo tjelesno zdravlje.
